title: Reggae
objective: After this level you can describe reggae and Bob Marley.
summary: Reggae came from western Kingston in the late 1960s, after ska and rocksteady, with choppy offbeat chords. Bob Marley carried it worldwide; UNESCO listed it as heritage in 2018.

cards.headline: UNESCO lists reggae as part of humanity's cultural heritage.
cards.body: In 2018, UNESCO added the reggae music of Jamaica to its list of the world's intangible cultural heritage. The style itself was young: it was born in Jamaica in the late 1960s, in marginalized communities of western Kingston. How did it travel so far, so fast?

cards.headline: Ska, rocksteady, reggae: and the offbeat
cards.body: Reggae grew out of earlier Jamaican styles: ska became rocksteady, which became reggae. Its signature is the offbeat. Drums and bass drive a heavy four-beat rhythm, while the rhythm guitar or keyboard plays short, choppy chords on the offbeats instead of the main beats. Listen for that chunk off the beat. It's reggae's fingerprint.

cards.headline: Bob Marley carries it worldwide
cards.body: Bob Marley, born in 1945 in Nine Miles, Jamaica, formed the Wailers in Trench Town with Peter Tosh and Bunny Wailer, writing songs for and about poor West Indians. Reggae's lyrics took on social and economic injustice, and through the Wailers it became linked with the Rastafari movement. After they signed with Island Records in 1972, their album Catch a Fire carried reggae worldwide. Marley died in 1981, at just 36.

cards.fact: In 1978, Bob Marley got two political rivals to join hands onstage.
cards.context: Jamaica was torn by political violence. At the One Love Peace Concert in Kingston, Marley brought Prime Minister Michael Manley and opposition leader Edward Seaga onstage and held their joined hands up high. For one night, a reggae concert was a peace summit.

cards.headline: Echoes in the Bronx
cards.body: Remember Kool Herc, the Kingston-born DJ with the loudest sound system in his Bronx neighborhood? Britannica counts hip-hop among the styles reggae influenced, along with dancehall. Herc carried Jamaica's sound-system parties and toasting north, and Bronx kids turned them into something new.

mascot.line: Kingston to the Bronx: sometimes a genre's family tree crosses an ocean.

questions.prompt: What did Bob Marley do at the One Love Peace Concert in Kingston?

options.label: Brought two rival political leaders onstage and joined their hands
Announced that the Wailers were breaking up
options.rationale: The concert is remembered for a gesture of peace, not a breakup.

options.label: Signed the Wailers' first deal with Island Records
options.rationale: The Island deal came in 1972, before the concert.

options.label: Played reggae live on the radio for the first time
options.rationale: The concert's famous moment was political, not a broadcast first.

questions.explanation: With Jamaica torn by political violence, Marley brought Michael Manley and Edward Seaga onstage and held their joined hands up high.

questions.prompt: What gives a reggae song its signature groove?

options.label: A bass drum on every beat of the bar
Short, choppy guitar or keyboard chords on the offbeats

questions.explanation: Over a heavy four-beat rhythm, the guitar or keyboard chops chords on the offbeats.

questions.prompt: Why does reggae's Jamaica belong in hip-hop's story?

options.label: Hip-hop's first records were made in Kingston studios
Bob Marley was one of the first hip-hop DJs
Kingston-born Kool Herc brought sound-system parties and toasting to the Bronx
UNESCO listed hip-hop and reggae together in 2018

questions.explanation: Herc's Jamaican sound-system and toasting roots fed Bronx hip-hop, one of the styles reggae influenced.
